title: MGX's $2B Binance investment settled in USD1
summary: Documented: MGX, chaired by Tahnoon bin Zayed, used WLF's weeks-old USD1 to settle its $2B Binance investment. WLF announced this on May 1, 2025 without disclosing that a Tahnoon-backed vehicle (Aryam Investment 1) had agreed in January 2025 to buy 49% of WLF, a stake the WSJ revealed in February 2026. USD1 jumped from about $128M to about $2.1B. The interest mechanism is real, but 'hundreds of millions' for the Trump family is a speculative cumulative upper bound (contemporaneous estimates: up to about $80M/yr on the $2B, shared beyond the family). WLF's 'unfair' quote could not be independently verified.

sub_claims.statement: WLF announced USD1 had been selected as the official stablecoin to close MGX's $2B investment in Binance.
sub_claims.finding: Zach Witkoff said this verbatim at TOKEN2049 Dubai on 2025-05-01. MGX had announced the $2B minority investment on 2025-03-12 without naming a stablecoin.

sub_claims.statement: USD1 was basically brand new at the time.
sub_claims.finding: USD1 was unveiled 2025-03-25, after MGX announced the Binance deal. Its market cap was under $130M on 2025-04-27. Forbes noted MGX cited a 'compliance history' the token barely had.

sub_claims.statement: The chairman of MGX is Tahnoon ('the spy').
sub_claims.finding: Official WAM releases show Tahnoon bin Zayed, UAE national security adviser, chairing MGX board meetings from 2024 to 2026.

sub_claims.statement: The WSJ links the MGX chairman to the 49% stake in WLF, which went undisclosed in the USD1 announcement.
sub_claims.finding: Per the WSJ (reported 2026-02-01), Aryam Investment 1, backed by Tahnoon, agreed in January 2025 to buy 49% of WLF for $500M ($250M upfront, about $187M to Trump-family entities). G42/MGX-linked figures took WLF board seats. The stake predates the May 2025 announcement and was not disclosed. The link runs through Aryam, not MGX itself, and MGX says it has not invested in WLF.

sub_claims.statement: WLF said it is 'unfair to hold a private company to arbitrary standards' and that MGX chose USD1 on its merits.
sub_claims.finding: The 'unfair/arbitrary standards' wording appears only in the video's own correspondence. WLF, MGX and Binance have all publicly said the choice was made on merits or by MGX alone.

sub_claims.statement: The deal catapulted USD1 from obscurity to a huge stablecoin.
sub_claims.finding: USD1 rose from about $128M to about $2.1B (+1,540%) around April 27-29, 2025 and became the 7th-largest stablecoin. It reached about $2.7B by October 2025 and more than $5B by early 2026, with Binance holding about 75-87% of supply.

sub_claims.statement: WLF earns interest on the reserves, potentially hundreds of millions for the Trump family over the presidency.
sub_claims.finding: The issuer keeps the reserve yield. Fortune estimated up to about $80M/yr on the $2B, and only if Binance holds the tokens. Over four years that is a few hundred million gross at best, not documented income. The Trump family receives only a share: DT Marks DEFI gets 75% of net protocol revenue, family equity is now about 38%, and Aryam holds 49%. MGX says it holds no USD1 and paid no fees. A Bloomberg-based estimate puts WLF's total 2026 USD1 income at about $147M.

corrections: Transcript says the WSJ associates the MGX chairman 'indirectly with his 49% stake'; the WSJ reported that Aryam Investment 1, a Tahnoon-backed vehicle distinct from MGX, agreed in January 2025 to buy 49% of WLF for $500M.
The quoted announcement was made by Zach Witkoff on 2025-05-01 at TOKEN2049 Dubai.

'Hundreds and hundreds of millions' is not a documented figure; contemporaneous estimates were up to about $80M/yr on the $2B, contingent on Binance holding the tokens, and shared with non-family WLF owners.
denials_and_context: WLF says MGX chose USD1 on its merits; per the video, WLF called holding a private company to such standards 'unfair'.
MGX says it chose USD1 for its reserve backing and compliance, does not hold USD1, paid no fees to WLF and has not invested in WLF.
Binance CEO Richard Teng says Binance was not involved in MGX's choice of stablecoin.
WLF and the White House told the WSJ that Trump was not involved in the Aryam deal and that it bought no policy influence; Trump denied knowledge of it.
Columbia's Omid Malekan noted that WLF earns no yield if Binance redeems the USD1 quickly; Bloomberg and Forbes later found Binance holding most USD1 supply.
Senators Warren and Merkley sought documents from MGX and Binance about the deal.
